ranking.note: Raised to P1: unlike the other regtest-only opcode proposals it resolves concrete consensus hazards (legacy sigop DoS, timewarp, 64-byte tx Merkle collisions) and is the soft-fork decision actually blocking project progress
Raised to P1 for consistency with #36149/#35744: same class of consequence (assertion abort, unrecoverable chainstate, false corruption forcing reindex)
Moved up: silently turning an unspendable script into anyone-can-spend is the sharpest of the corruption-handling fixes in this band
Grouped with the other corruption-surfacing fixes (#35714, #36280) since they harden the same invariant
Moved up to sit with the other storage-error-handling fixes; a silently stuck node is a reliability consequence, and the stalled approach debate does not lower priority
Moved up: largest measured validation speedup on the list (1.5x reindex, 1.13x IBD) felt by all node operators
Placed below the measured IBD speedup since its benefit is latency/contention and it is still at concept stage
Lowered to P2 to match the other proposed-opcode implementations (#31989, #32247, #36122); no activation parameters and no decision pressure distinguishing it from them
Ordered after the corruption and performance fixes; regtest-only covenant testing is strategic but not category-critical
Placed above #29491 because it is the stated prerequisite for that work and separately fixes a script-cache bypass
Moved down: the speedup is real but gated on unmerged upstream secp256k1 work and on #32575
Moved well down: motivation is a kernel/external-reader limitation, and rewriting mandatory block-index persistence is a large new hazard rather than a fix to an existing one
Moved up sharply: author demonstrates reproducible silent destruction of block data down to height 0, the most severe consequence in the P3 group
Moved up to lead the localized-speedup group; measured IBD and assumeutxo gains affect all users
Lowered to P3 for consistency with the other localized speedups (#35195, #33637): ~10% on template validation for miners only
Moved down: benefit accrues to external kernel consumers, not to node validation behavior, placing it below in-tree hardening and refactors
Moved down: fixes one intermittent test race and adds a kernel-consumer capability; no production validation change

inconsistencies: Soft-fork/opcode proposals were banded inconsistently when assessed alone (#29247 P1 vs #31989/#32247/#36122 P2 for the same kind of regtest-only proposal). They are now all P2 except #35793, which is P1 because it fixes real consensus hazards and is the fork decision under active project consideration.
Chain: #35731 is explicitly built on top of #35714 (flush-error notification invariant depends on the flush-failure write stop). Review #35714 first; #35731 loses most of its point on its own.
Chain: #35646 removes M_ERROR from ValidationState and is described as unblocking #35570's return-by-value refactor. Review #35646 before #35570.
Chain: #32575 is stated preparation for #29491 (Schnorr batch verification); #29491 additionally waits on unmerged secp256k1 PRs 1134/1789. Review #32575 first.
Chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) sits on top of #35793 (BIP 54) and cannot be evaluated until BIP 54's rules are settled.

Same area, overlapping: #35938 (fail instead of writing a null XOR key) and #33324 (resumable reobfuscation of existing block files) both change block-file XOR key handling. Review #35938 first, since it prevents data loss, and check that #33324's rewrite path respects the new missing-key failure.

Overlapping problem space: #35071 (persist reindex progress) and #33854 (assumevalid ignored during reindex) both rework reindex control flow, and reviewers on #33854 note it complicates offline reindex. They should be read together; #35071 is the lower-risk of the two.

#35906, #36066 and #35569 are all increments of the #35904 stateless-validation modularization. #35906 carries the actual testability payoff; #36066 and #35569 are mechanical and should not consume review attention ahead of it.
#35751 depends on the CoinsViewOverlay introduced in #35295; confirm that landed before reviewing.

#32427 (block tree DB replacement) and #35187/#35557 are kernel-motivated but touch mandatory validation structures. #32427 in particular is a kernel-API-driven rewrite of mandatory block-index persistence and would be easier to review if the storage change were separable from the kernel reader use case.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small set of crash/corruption bugs and the BIP 54 decision at P1; corruption-handling hardening, measured IBD/validation performance work and the proposed-opcode implementations at P2; localized speedups, invariant tightening and modularization steps at P3; pure janitorial refactors and the downstream-only fix at P4. Drafts, stale threads and NACKed approaches (#36244, #35003, #32427, #35861) were not penalized.
